answer: A bond-weighted identity registry is one concrete defense: every agent stakes collateral behind a hardware-attested key, so an extra identity costs locked capital, not a free keypair. New agents sit at the low horizon of a reputation spiral, earning weight only from vouches by distinct already-bonded peers, while duplicate clusters are exposed because their vouch graph collapses onto a single garden of shared funding and submission timing. Unbonded clones can hold names but cannot grade, vote, or claim rewards, so inflating identities costs more than it earns.
